items.title: Panthers' Sandis Vilmanis exits game after hit by Capitals' Tom Wilson
items.desc: Panthers forward Sandis Vilmanis was shaken up after a hit by Washington's Tom Wilson, who was given a major penalty for boarding and a game misconduct.

stories.take:
The scary part first: Sandis Vilmanis left Florida's game in Washington after a hit by Tom Wilson, who got a boarding major and a game misconduct, ESPN reports. There's no word yet on Vilmanis's condition, and we won't guess.

What the Panthers could lose is more than a depth forward's 12:32 a night. Vilmanis has seven points in 16 games, but the bigger number is what happens with him on the ice: 63% of the five-on-five expected goals, about 14 percentage points better than Florida does without him. He's the kind of player who makes a third line work. Wilson, meanwhile, has a long history with the league's Department of Player Safety, and we'd expect this hit to get a look. Washington won the game 4-3 without him, mostly at even strength.

items.title: Two NHL players placed on waivers for Nov. 7
items.desc: Atro Leppanen and James Reimer have both been officially put on waivers on Saturday.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Atro Leppanen and James Reimer were officially placed on waivers on Saturday. New York Post reporter Mollie Walker posted earlier in the week that Reimer would still back up Dylan Garand that night, calling the move "next step in Joonas Korpisalo's impending return."

Our numbers say the Rangers aren't giving up much. Reimer has played one game so far this season, stopping .625 of the shots he faced. By goals saved above expected, which measures how many goals a goalie stopped compared with what an average goalie would have allowed on the same shots, he sits at -1.96. That is a tiny sample, but it echoes last year: in 14 games he finished at -1.67, so he has now cost his team goals relative to the chances he faced in both stretches. A backup who gives back close to two goals in a single start is a real risk when the starter needs a night off, and the waiver move suggests the Rangers see it the same way. For fantasy, Reimer holds no value, and the one number worth watching is how New York's goaltending looks once Korpisalo is back and the backup job is settled.

stories.desc: Wilson drilled the Florida defenseman from behind into the boards, resulting in a major penalty and a game misconduct.

items.title: Capitals’ Wilson ejected for boarding Panthers’ Vilmanis
items.desc: Wilson drilled the Florida defenseman from behind into the boards, resulting in a major penalty and a game misconduct.

stories.take:
Tom Wilson's afternoon ended early: Daily Faceoff reports he drove Sandis Vilmanis into the boards from behind and was given a major and a game misconduct. (Their report calls Vilmanis a defenseman; he plays forward for Florida.)

The question now is whether the league adds games. Wilson has been suspended before, more than once, and repeat offenders get longer bans. If he sits, Washington loses a 17-minute winger who hasn't been scoring (two goals on 4.97 expected) but is still a fixture on the top six, at 55.6% of the five-on-five expected goals. The Capitals showed Saturday they can survive a game without him, coming back from 2-1 down to win 4-3. A week or two without him is a different test.

items.title: Bruins place James Hagens on injured reserve
items.desc: The Bruins have called up Mike Eyssimont from their AHL affiliate, the Providence Bruins.

stories.take:
Boston has put James Hagens on injured reserve and called up Mike Eyssimont from Providence, Daily Faceoff reports. The reason hasn't been made public.

It's a loss the Bruins will feel. Hagens, the seventh overall pick in 2025, has 12 points (six goals) in 17 games while playing just 13:20 a night, a rate of 3.17 points per 60 that most veteran forwards would take. Our caution: his on-ice luck is running hot, with his teammates scoring well above their chances while he's out there, so some cooling was coming anyway. The bigger point is that Boston's 12-4-1 start rests on goaltending (12.6 goals saved beyond expected) more than on play, with the expected goals split close to even. Losing scoring depth makes that margin thinner.

items.title: Panthers’ Anton Lundell day-to-day with undisclosed injury
items.desc: Lundell has four goals and six points in 16 games with the Panthers in 2026-27.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports Anton Lundell is day-to-day with an undisclosed injury, and the outlet puts his line at four goals and six points through 16 games.

That line undersells him. At 5-on-5, Florida has taken 57.73% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Lundell on the ice, 5.19 points better than without him. The scoring hasn't followed because his linemates keep missing: his on-ice luck number sits at -5.17, meaning the goals while he plays trail the chances by about five. Last season he had 44 points in 64 games.

For a 9-5-2 Panthers team, a short absence costs them a center who drives play more than his points show. Day-to-day is the good version of this news.

items.title: Blues recall Logan Mailloux from conditioning assignment ahead of potential season debut
items.desc: Mailloux suffered a hand injury during a fight in the preseason.

stories.take:
Logan Mailloux is closer to his first game of the season. Daily Faceoff reports the Blues have recalled him from a conditioning assignment, after a hand injury he picked up in a preseason fight kept him out.

St. Louis could use what he does. The Blues are 7-7-2 and have taken only 48.59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against), and their goalies have been covering for it, allowing 2.46 fewer goals than the shots deserved. A right-shot defenseman whose game is moving the puck forward, Mailloux was Montreal's first-round pick in 2021.

One debut won't change a team's shot share. If he sticks, though, watch whether St. Louis starts spending a little less time in its own end.

items.title: Sabres place Jack Rathbone on waivers
items.desc: Rathbone has yet to suit up in either an NHL or AHL game this season due to injury.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Sabres have placed Jack Rathbone on waivers. The outlet notes he hasn't played a game in the NHL or AHL this season because of injury.

This is a roster move more than a hockey one. Buffalo's blue line has settled: Rasmus Dahlin and Mattias Samuelsson have played about 163 minutes together at 5-on-5, and Owen Power with Olen Zellweger nearly 135, the second pair controlling 56% of the expected goals (chance quality). Even healthy, Rathbone would be competing for a depth spot behind them.

The Sabres sit 8-5-3 with an even 49.98% share of expected goals. If another team claims him, it gets a puck-moving defenseman for nothing. If nobody does, Buffalo can send him to the AHL, where he can finally get games.

items.title: Robby Fabbri signs tryout contract with AHL’s Hamilton Hammers
items.desc: The Hammers also signed former Dallas Stars prospect Antonio Stranges to a PTO.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports Robby Fabbri has signed a professional tryout with the AHL's Hamilton Hammers, who also brought in former Dallas Stars prospect Antonio Stranges on a PTO.

For Fabbri, the 2014 first-round pick of the St. Louis Blues, this is a road back rather than a destination: a tryout lets him show he is healthy and sharp without a contract attached. Stranges never broke through in Dallas, and the Stars haven't needed him to. They are 9-5-2 and have allowed just 36 goals on 44.05 expected, while their shooters have scored about four fewer goals than their chances deserved.

Neither signing moves an NHL needle today. Both are worth a glance in a month, when injuries start to pile up around the league.

stories.title: Undeterred by Robertson whiff, Kraken are big-game hunting in trade market
stories.desc: Looking to level up, the Kraken would like to find a scoring winger or top-four defenseman.

items.title: Undeterred by Robertson whiff, Kraken are big-game hunting in trade market
items.desc: Looking to level up, the Kraken would like to find a scoring winger or top-four defenseman.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Kraken are still shopping big after missing on Robertson, with a scoring winger or a top-four defenseman on the list.

Here's why that makes sense even at 9-5-1. Seattle has taken 45.4% of the expected goals (the quality of chances both ways), so it has been outchanced most nights. The record leans on finishing: 52 goals on 42.1 expected, a 9.9-goal cushion that rarely survives a full season. The goalies aren't the reason they're winning either; they've allowed 2.36 more goals than the shots deserved.

So the shopping list fits. A winger who creates chances and a defenseman who limits them both attack the actual gap. Standing pat and hoping the shooting holds is the riskier path for this front office.

items.title: Sabres’ Ryan McLeod, Louis Crevier healthy scratches Friday against Columbus
items.desc: Jiri Kulich and Conor Timmins are expected to enter the Sabres’ lineup in Friday’s game.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reported Ryan McLeod and Louis Crevier as healthy scratches for Friday against Columbus, with Jiri Kulich and Conor Timmins coming in.

McLeod's case is more bad luck than bad play. He has one goal and three points in 15 games after 54 points last season, but his on-ice luck reads -8.59: the Sabres have scored about eight and a half fewer goals with him out there than their chances earned. He's still one of the fastest skaters in the league, 98th percentile for top speed.

Crevier is harder to defend: Buffalo has taken 40.08% of the expected goals with him on at 5-on-5, 12.84 points worse than without him. Kulich (56.8% and +8.04 relative in nine games) has earned the look. McLeod's numbers argue for a quick return; Crevier's argue for patience.

items.title: Fantasy hockey trade suggestions: Guide to the luckiest and unluckiest shooters
items.desc: Are these hot (or cold) starts sustainable? We look at the extreme shooting percentages and trades to make.

stories.take:
ESPN's fantasy desk went looking for the luckiest and unluckiest shooters this week, and our numbers point the same way on four names.

Mark Scheifele has 3 goals on 6.74 expected (chance quality) after 36 last season; gaps like that usually close. Juraj Slafkovsky is the same story, 2 goals on 5.66 expected and among the hardest shots in the league. Patrick Kane, 1 goal on 3.12, is less clear-cut: Chicago has taken just 35.47% of the expected goals with him on at 5-on-5, so the bounce may be smaller.

Logan Cooley is the flip side. He has 11 goals on 6.01 expected, and 14 of his 21 points have come on the power play. Our form check still calls his hot run earned, because the chances are real. The finishing rate is the part that won't last.

items.title: Oilers' Brett Epp dresses as full-time emergency backup goalie
items.desc: The Oilers became the first NHL team to dress a full-time emergency backup goalie Thursday night for their game against against Anaheim.

stories.take:
ESPN reports that the Oilers became the first NHL team to dress a full-time emergency backup goalie on Thursday night against Anaheim, with Brett Epp in that role. The headline and summary don't say more than that, so we won't guess at the reason.

The more useful question is what the goaltending behind the story looks like. EDM sit at 11-2-3 with 25 points in 16 games, and their share of expected goals (a measure of chance quality for versus against) is 52 percent so far this season. They've scored 18.1 goals more than expected, but their goalies are 2.4 goals below expected in saves. So the results lean on finishing, not on the crease. At five-on-five, expected goal share drops to 49 percent, which means the edge comes from special teams. The power play generates 0.88 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allows 0.52. If goaltending stays shaky, depth in net matters more than usual.

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that Connor Hellebuyck, now with the Devils, addressed Jets fans for the first time since the trade, breaking his silence in an Instagram post about his decision to request a move out of Winnipeg.

The numbers say New Jersey is doing fine around him. The Devils are 10-5-0 and generate 58.6 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) so far this season, with a strong 5-on-5 share of 58 percent. Hellebuyck's own start is the soft spot: three games, a .900 save percentage, and goals saved above expected of -0.54, meaning he has let in about half a goal more than an average goalie would have on the same shots. That is a tiny sample, and last season he was 3.43 goals better than expected over 57 games. Winnipeg, at 5-8-3, creates only 45.7 percent of the expected goals and has scored 9.6 fewer goals than its chances suggest. Its goaltending is roughly average (-0.1), so the Jets' problems sit mostly in play and finishing, not in net.

items.title: Dallas Stars GM Jim Nill Is Facing A Major Test With Jason Robertson's Next Contract
items.desc: Dallas Stars GM Jim Nill has managed his team's salary cap situation very well, but Jason Robertson's success could blow up their cap structure. How will the winger's next contract play out?

stories.take:
The Hockey News reports that Stars GM Jim Nill has handled Dallas's cap well, but that Jason Robertson's production could strain the structure when his next contract comes due. The same day, NHL.com's Tom Gulitti posted that Robertson scored the ninth-fastest hat trick to start a period in NHL history.

Our numbers say the production is real, if a touch hot. Robertson has 8 goals and 18 points in 15 games so far this season, and he's 2.31 goals above what his chances would predict. Expected goals measure the quality of chances, and his own sit at 5.7, so some of those 8 goals are finishing luck. The underlying play still holds up: DAL controls 56 percent of the expected goals at five-on-five when he's on the ice, and the team's share of the play is about 7 points better with him than without him. That's the kind of impact a team pays for, which is Nill's problem. Robertson went from 45 goals and 96 points last season, and he was drafted 39th overall in 2017, so the price has climbed steeply. DAL is 9-5-1, but its goals are 2.5 below expected and its goalies are 6.1 saved above expected, so the Stars need Robertson's driving to stay steady.
